text:
maria: Heads-up — proposing a small Grafana dashboard to catch short GPU power transients (sub-1m), PDU battery draw patterns, and overlay maintenance/ops windows. Idea: lightweight, high-signal panels we can ship to staging.
kevin: love it. can you sketch the core panels?
maria: six panels: 1) transient heatmap (1s->1m buckets), 2) per-GPU power sparkline with throttle markers, 3) PDU battery SOC + discharge rate, 4) thermal correlation (temp vs power), 5) memory usage vs util scatter, 6) maintenance/annotation timeline overlay.
anya: for the transient heatmap, use shorter scrape for irate. sample promql: 
```
sum by (gpu) (irate(nvidia_gpu_power_draw_watts[30s]))
```
filter by rack label for the rack panel.
jamal: for throttles, we have a label on the GPU exporter `throttle_state`. quick query: 
```
max_over_time(nvidia_gpu_throttle_state[2m]) by (gpu) > 0
```
pat: watch alert noise — short transients will be noisy if we make alerts too eager. propose recording rule to pre-aggregate spikes and then alert on sustained repeats.
vishal: what about annotating scheduled PDUs and firmware updates? that would explain false positives. we should add an annotations import from incidents -> grafana.
maria: yes — plan: annotate via /api/annotations with `source=ops` and `tags=maintenance,pdu`. snippet: 
```
POST /api/annotations
{ "time": 1610000000000, "text": "PDU firmware update - rack 4", "tags": ["maintenance","pdu"] }
```
kevin: alert tuning suggestion: record `gpu_power_spike_rate` as: 
```
rate_high_spike = sum by (rack) (increase((nvidia_gpu_power_draw_watts > 400)[5m]))
```
then alert when `rate_high_spike > 3` for 10m. (avoid single-blip alarms).
anya: question on dashboard layout: do we want per-region rows? some regions have different PDU setups.
maria: yes — row per region, then rack panels inside. keeps dashboards readable. default landing should be `region=us-west` filter.
jamal: panel-level options: use series overrides to dim idle GPUs and highlight ones crossing 85% of rated power. small color thresholds.
pat: ops: when this lands to prod, can we gate alerts behind on-call rotation? otherwise paging for weird PDUs at 2am.
vishal: +1. add an alert annotation to suppress during `ops:maintenance` window via silence API.
sre-bot: dashboard pushed to staging: https://grafana.internal/d/7d9c3e7/gpu-power-transients (uid: 7d9c3e7). deployment id: deploy-8721.
maria: testing plan: 1) run for 72h in staging, 2) seed some synthetic transients via `stress-power` tool, 3) collect false-positive stats, 4) iterate thresholds.
kevin: can you drop the Prometheus recording rules and an example alert rule in the PR? I'll review.
maria: will do — prepping PR now. sample alert rule to include in the PR: 
```yaml
groups:
- name: gpu-power-rules
  rules:
  - alert: GPUHighTransientRate
    expr: rate_high_spike > 3
    for: 10m
    labels:
      severity: warning
    annotations:
      summary: "High transient power events in {{ $labels.rack }}"
```
anya: also add a dashboard link from the `gpu-fleet` Confluence page. easier for on-call.
pat: FYI: we should avoid adding raw `increase()` alerts on raw watt metrics — use normalized percent-of-rated-power to account for model differences.
maria: good call — will normalize by `gpu_power_max_watts`. updated promql example: 
```
sum by (gpu) (irate(nvidia_gpu_power_draw_watts[30s]) / gpu_power_max_watts) * 100
```
jamal: thumbs-up. when PR is up ping #eng-oncall and I'll run the synthetic tests.
maria: thanks everyone. I'll post PR link and a staging screenshot shortly. :thumbsup:
